races.name: William Hill Silver Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Theoryofeverything
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who stays on from off the pace; O'Meara/Hart combination at Beverley is worth noting, and his sim-going record (1W2P at soft/heavy-adjacent) is the most relevant figure — 22 days fresh is ideal, but he wants the trip to be truly run to suit his one-paced style.

runners_data.name: Impartiality
runners_data.note: Has placed twice on soft going and handles the trip (2nd over 10f soft last time), so the conditions are not a concern; races prominently and Shane Gray, a Beverley regular, will try to secure a forward berth, but six rivals with similar intentions makes that task harder.

runners_data.name: Wahdan
runners_data.note: Jake Dickson claims 5lb which helps against a field of this grade; his sim-going record is thin (0W1P in 3 runs) and recent form shows a string of mid-table efforts — likely to race hold-up despite a nominally prominent style tag and needs the trip to expose tiring rivals.

runners_data.name: Tiger
runners_data.note: Has won and placed over 10f and 12f on soft ground (four runs in similar conditions, 0W2P), making him one of the more genuinely soft-ground-suited runners here; Paul Mulrennan is a strong booking and this hold-up profile suits the expected race shape well.

runners_data.name: Jez Bomb
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground recently and has back-to-back wins in his recent record, though only one run on soft — 14 days since last run is tight but he is clearly in form; will race prominently and is one of the runners most likely to actually secure a handy position.

runners_data.name: Fox Avatar
runners_data.note: Roger Varian runner who won over 12f on Flat and handles varying surfaces; just one run in soft-adjacent conditions, but PJ McDonald takes over and the form includes placed efforts; will race prominently and is capable if he gets the right trip and a clean run through.

runners_data.name: Kind Of Kiss
runners_data.note: 41 days off since last run, and recent form is moderate (three consecutive missing efforts); soft going is not proven to be a positive and this is a stiff task at OR 80 — Oisin Orr keeps the ride but this hold-up type needs pace and gaps that may not materialise.

runners_data.name: Oratorical
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has been off 115 days — the longest layoff in the field — which is a clear concern; Laura Pearson rides and is a competent claimer, but the soft ground and longer absence after a disappointing run last time make this a tough assignment for the youngster.

runners_data.name: Galyx
runners_data.note: Two wins on soft/heavy going in his record make the conditions a genuine positive angle here; George Bass takes over and Channon sends runners to Beverley in form (2/23 T14); races prominently and, if Bay Of Myths is squeezed out, Galyx could find a berth closer to the pace than his nominal midfield position suggests.

runners_data.name: Amancio
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner whose entire race map revolves around this horse — 63 days off but two wins on soft including over 9f soft and a Flat win over 17f soft — the stamina base is strong; Tom Eaves will stride on and face no pressure, making his own running entirely.

runners_data.name: Per Contra
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has been pushed into a midfield mapping because of the volume of rear-positioned types in this field — his actual role will be to race from off the pace; Tim Easterby sends him fit (LR 24d) and David Allan is capable, but recent form (no wins or places in five on varying surfaces) is hard to enthuse over.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Myths
runners_data.note: Just two career runs but a win at Sandown over 10f (soft-adjacent) and a third at Goodwood — experience is minimal and 132 days off adds to the unknown element; naturally wants to race prominently but the number of forward-going rivals means she is likely to find herself racing further back than suits.

runners_data.name: Mudita
runners_data.note: Three-year-old on a low OR of 67 who is naturally a hold-up type displaced into midfield on this map; ran just 8 days ago and the quick turnaround on soft ground over a longer trip than her best form suggests is a concern — Fahey sends her fit but this is a competitive handicap debut step up.

races.paceDynamic: Amancio is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just 63 days off and a strong record on soft going (2W3P in similar conditions), will dictate from the front at a pace he controls entirely — on soft ground at Beverley over 1m2f that means a measured, stamina-testing gallop rather than a scorching tempo. With no genuine challenger willing or able to pressure him, Amancio should establish a comfortable lead and grind out a rhythm that will drain the field rather than sharpen it. Impartiality, Jez Bomb, Fox Avatar, Oratorical, and Galyx are all prominent-leaning types, but this field holds more horses wanting to race forward than the map can honestly accommodate — Jez Bomb and Fox Avatar are best placed to actually secure prominent berths behind Amancio, while Bay Of Myths, despite being a natural prominent runner, is likely to find itself squeezed further back than ideal. This race shape — a lone leader setting a controlled, grinding soft-ground pace — strongly favours confirmed hold-up and staying horses who can be produced late with one sustained run, rewarding stamina and tactical patience over tactical positioning or early speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Amancio Controls, Stays-On Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Amancio leads uncontested and the soft ground makes this a thorough stamina test.
scenarios.body: Amancio sets a sustainable pace that stretches the field in the home straight, and genuine stayers who can be produced with a single sustained run pick off the tiring prominents. The soft going amplifies the stamina premium, making this the dominant shape given the single-source pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Land A Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Jez Bomb or Fox Avatar track Amancio closely and benefit from a falsely-run gallop.
scenarios.body: A controlled pace means those sitting just behind the leader avoid wasting energy and arrive at the straight full of running, with the held-up horses caught too far back to close. This suits a horse with tactical speed and a recent win to its name rather than a true stayer.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Amancio goes too slow early then quickens, leaving hold-up horses with ground to make up but a clear late run.
scenarios.body: On soft ground at Beverley the home turn can compress the field and create a late surge if the pace has been gentle enough to leave horses fresh, rewarding those with the widest closing kick. True hold-up types who have been running from their natural position — Tiger, Theoryofeverything — are best suited to deliver in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Muddled Finish
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for position among the prominent types causes interference and no horse gets a clear run.
scenarios.body: Multiple horses competing for prominent ground disrupt the expected order, and the race degenerates into a scramble in the straight where luck in running becomes a factor. Shorter-priced contenders who need clean runs are most at risk, and opportunistic hold-up horses that find gaps could benefit.

watchPoints.text: Amancio — if Tom Eaves is allowed to dictate completely unchallenged from the front on soft ground, the controlled pace he sets will be the single biggest factor shaping this race; watch whether any prominent runner (Jez Bomb or Fox Avatar) elects to press him.

Bay Of Myths and Jez Bomb — both natural prominent types competing for the same limited forward positions behind Amancio; early crowding between them in the first furlong could compromise both runners and open the race up for hold-up horses.

Oratorical — 115 days off is the longest layoff in the field and the step onto soft ground at Beverley after a string of disappointing runs makes this a watch-not-back situation; Laura Pearson may find it hard to land a blow if the race is run at a true test-of-stamina pace.

Tiger — one of the more genuinely soft-ground-proven hold-up horses in the field (4 runs in similar going, 0W2P); Mulrennan will be patient and the question is whether the race is truly run slowly enough from the front to leave a strong late run available.

Mudita — ran only 8 days ago and steps up sharply in trip and class; the quick bounce on soft going is a notable watch flag, and Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim softens the weight burden but does not resolve the stamina or recovery question.

races.name: William Hill Beverley Bullet Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Washington Heights
runners_data.note: Strong claims here having won over this C/D/G combination already this season; soft-ground record is modest in absolute terms (1 win from 15 soft runs) but his recent 2nd on soft is encouraging, and Tom Eaves should get him the position right behind Jm Jungle that matters most in this shape.

runners_data.name: Ain't Nobody
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up sprinter for Kevin Ryan — headgear note (p) suggests he is managed carefully — but his recent form shows a wall of double-digit finishing positions on soft, and 9 days since last run for a horse who needs things to fall right is a concern in this shape.

runners_data.name: Al Shabab Storm
runners_data.note: Won a Sandown 5f on standard AW recently and has soft-ground placed form, but his true nature as a prominent racer means he will be shuffled into an enforced midfield here given the traffic ahead of him; the 65-day absence since that win adds another question mark.

runners_data.name: Badri
runners_data.note: A remarkable recent record with three wins from six including back-to-back victories, but all that winning form has come on good or better ground — his sole soft run produced a distant 13th, and being unable to get his natural prominent berth in this field compounds the concern significantly.

runners_data.name: Jm Jungle
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner and the pivotal horse in understanding this race's shape; headgear (b) and soft-ground form (1W from 5 soft runs) back his chance of controlling this, though his recent form string (4-9-0-3-5-7) shows he does not always convert from the front.

runners_data.name: Shagraan
runners_data.note: Won on soft and placed on soft in his five most recent runs, giving him strong going credentials; PJ McDonald secures the ride for Clive Cox who has been in excellent form (5/24 over 14 days), and Shagraan's natural prominent style means he should be able to take up a genuine position behind the leader.

runners_data.name: Argentine Tango
runners_data.note: The youngest runner in the field at three, and his only soft-ground win came here on this track over 5f — a course-and-distance soft angle worth noting — but his naturally prominent style means he is likely to be crowded out of position, and the 30-day break is not a concern for a Tim Easterby sprint type.

runners_data.name: Beaujolais Nouveau
runners_data.note: Headgear (v) fitted and a hold-up horse by style whose five most recent runs have all come over 6f — stepping back to 5f on soft ground at Beverley is a meaningful challenge, and his going form (0W0P from 2 soft runs) offers little encouragement despite winning at 6f on good ground.

runners_data.name: Elegant Erin
runners_data.note: A veteran at nine years old who has won twice from four soft-ground runs, giving her the best going strike-rate among the hold-up horses; her last run was 58 days ago which is worth monitoring, but she handles this going and has placed credentials on 5f, even if her style leaves her dependent on others doing her work.

runners_data.name: Fluorescence
runners_data.note: Listed in the data as having a sole soft-ground run (1 win from 12), but that one run was a soft-ground victory over this distance which is a meaningful data point; her natural prominent style means she too will be absorbed into a crowded midfield, blunting a profile that would otherwise look more compelling.

runners_data.name: Heavenly Heather
runners_data.note: Has soft-ground placed form (2nd) in her recent past and has been busy (third run in nine days) which could be a freshness concern; her natural prominent style gives her a better chance than the redistributed horses of getting close to the pace, but the going form (0W0P from 2 soft runs) and recent below-par runs (5-4-2-6-0-0) make it hard to be enthusiastic.

races.paceDynamic: Jm Jungle is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no significant challenger for the lead, he should settle into a controllable, energy-efficient gallop from the front on soft ground at Beverley — a scenario that historically suits the pace-setter at this track where the rise to the finish line can expose those who have been held up. Washington Heights and Shagraan are the most likely duo to press him from prominent positions just off the shoulder, giving the race a defined shape: a genuine but uncontested lead, a small group of chasers, and the hold-up horses — Ain't Nobody, Elegant Erin, and Beaujolais Nouveau — likely too far back to land a telling blow on ground that will sap late momentum. This field contains more prominent types than can realistically secure their natural position: Al Shabab Storm, Badri, Argentine Tango, Fluorescence, and Heavenly Heather are all genuine prominent racers who will be shuffled back into an enforced midfield, with Washington Heights and Shagraan best placed to actually hold the positions directly behind Jm Jungle. The race shape strongly favours horses who can track the pace within the first two or three lengths and sustain their effort up the stiff Beverley finish — prominent-position types who can get their natural berth, not those forced to race out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jm Jungle Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Jm Jungle dictates an uncontested soft lead and the forcing pack cannot get close enough to apply meaningful pressure.
scenarios.body: Jm Jungle bowls along in front at a measured pace that suits a soft-ground 5f, conserving energy before the uphill finish where rivals deep in the pack face a do-or-die challenge; the horses best placed to challenge are those who tracked him in the first two or three lengths — Washington Heights and Shagraan — whose positions allow them to pounce without wasting reserves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Peg Him Back
scenarios.trigger: If Washington Heights and Shagraan apply sustained pressure to Jm Jungle from early on, forcing a stronger pace that tests his stamina on soft ground.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested pace develops with two or three horses racing tight to the leader throughout, turning the race into a stamina examination on soft ground where the first three home are likely to be those who raced close to the action from the start; Washington Heights, with soft-ground form and a clear prominent role, is ideally suited, while Shagraan's Listed-class form on soft gives him every chance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Splits Them
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves strong enough to string out the field and a horse with natural pace racing from a midfield position delivers a sustained run to cut them all down.
scenarios.body: The enforced midfield cluster of displaced prominent types — Badri in particular, who has won five of his last six when getting his position — benefits if the early pace is fierce enough to set up a strong-finishing effort; Badri's extraordinary recent record of wins on good ground is a concern on soft, but he is the one redistributed horse whose class and finishing habit make him a genuine threat even from an unfavoured position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If an unusually strong pace collapses the prominent group and the back-markers find soft ground no barrier to a late rattle.
scenarios.body: Ain't Nobody and Elegant Erin are genuine hold-up horses, but soft ground at Beverley notoriously punishes those who need to produce a run from the rear over just 5f; this scenario requires a combination of a truly strong pace and exceptional late energy that the going makes highly unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Jm Jungle's early sectionals are key — if he is allowed to stride clear uncontested in the first furlong, the race is likely to be run to suit him and Washington Heights; watch whether Shagraan or Washington Heights apply any pressure from the outset.

The cluster of displaced prominent types — Al Shabab Storm, Badri, Fluorescence, and Argentine Tango — will all be jostling for position in the early stages; a scrimmage or interference among this group in the first two furlongs could compromise multiple runners simultaneously.

Badri's soft-ground form is strikingly poor (13th of 15 on his sole soft run) — if the going is testing rather than just soft, his strong recent form on good may count for very little and punters relying on his current momentum should factor this in.

Elegant Erin at nine years old has a live each-way claim on soft — her two soft-ground wins show she handles the conditions better than most hold-up types here, and if the pace proves stronger than expected she is the hold-up horse most capable of benefiting.

Both Kevin Ryan runners (Washington Heights and Ain't Nobody) share the same jockey and trainer with an identical 14-day record (2/31) — confirm stable intentions pre-race, as Washington Heights appears the yard's more natural fit for this race shape and going combination.

races.name: Churchill Tyres EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cheeky Chesca
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's confirmed front-runner with soft-ground form (3rd at Carlisle on soft), has proven 5f stamina, goes fresh off 13 days, and with no pace rival she sets every fraction — the race is built around her.

runners_data.name: Dawn's Gift
runners_data.note: One run to date, sixth at Goodwood on good — a natural hold-up filly whose style is compromised immediately by the five-furlong trip and large field; her chance hinges on soft ground collapsing the pace late, which is uncertain.

runners_data.name: Dorothea Hope
runners_data.note: Three runs all on good at 5f in maidens, improving each time to finish 4th; another genuine closer whose natural game plan is squeezed by the race shape, so she will need late chaos to fire.

runners_data.name: Eleven Eighty Two
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's twice-placed prominent runner at 6f on good is stepping back to 5f and stepping up in ground — the drop in trip is a query but she maps to the ideal second position and her recent placed efforts show she can compete.

runners_data.name: Floral Maid
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison debutante with unknown style and going — Ellison can place a first-timer to win and 5f soft at Beverley suits a naturally quick two-year-old, but the absence of any data makes assessment speculative.

runners_data.name: Get On That Baby
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby newcomer on debut — yard sends them ready and the trainer partnership has a solid 5f soft strike-rate, but style and trip suitability are entirely unknown until the stalls open.

runners_data.name: Last Dandelion
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' hold-up filly with six starts and a best of 2nd at 6f; drops back to 5f and faces the same redistribution squeeze as the other closers — running out of her natural position reduces her winning chance here.

runners_data.name: Picnic Princess
runners_data.note: Fahey yard debutante — Richard Fahey is lethal with sharp two-year-olds at Beverley and on soft, so this filly merits respect on stable angle alone, though without form her style and suitability are unconfirmed.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Voyage
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan newcomer and the trainer knows how to target five-furlong soft maidens with first-timers; Tom Eaves gets the ride which is a useful booking, making this one of the more respected unknowns in the field.

runners_data.name: Pocket Change
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's filly returns after 126 days off following an eighth-place debut at 5f on good; the long layoff is a concern, she is flagged as a fader, and a hard ground debut offers no soft-ground confidence.

runners_data.name: Purrista
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's hold-up filly runs back after only four days, showing 3rd and 5th form over 5f on good — the quick return is notable, but soft ground and the five-furlong trip are queries for a closer who needs more cut than she is likely to get.

runners_data.name: Serenity Bay
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's hold-up type drops from 6-7f on good/standard to 5f soft — the combination of a sharp trip, taxing ground, a 40-day break, and a fading tendency makes this look like a tough ask for her to show her best.

runners_data.name: Suenicora Star
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's second string after two runs including a 5th at 5f on good; a hold-up filly with limited form, soft ground is unproven, and her position in the race map offers no tactical advantage.

races.paceDynamic: Cheeky Chesca is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press her for the lead, she will dictate a controlled, unchallenged tempo down Beverley's straight five furlongs on soft ground — conditions that will bleed stamina late but reward anything that can travel kindly close to the pace. Behind her, Eleven Eighty Two is the most credible prominent horse and should settle just off the leader's quarters, while the bulk of the field — Dawn's Gift, Dorothea Hope, Last Dandelion, Pocket Change, Purrista, and Serenity Bay — are true hold-up types crammed into a midfield that offers them little natural space to express their style over five furlongs. The pace shape is single-source and sustainable rather than strong, which creates a smooth gallop likely to reward the prominent holder rather than the genuine closer. This race favours the early-position profile: horses who can race within a length or two of Cheeky Chesca without burning energy will be best placed when the ground saps stamina inside the final furlong. The field contains more hold-up types than the race map can honestly accommodate; Dawn's Gift, Dorothea Hope, and Last Dandelion are all natural closers redistributed to midfield on the map, but in practice none is likely to secure a true hold-up berth in a 13-runner five-furlong dash on soft — Cheeky Chesca and Eleven Eighty Two are by far the most likely to actually get their position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cheeky Chesca Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Cheeky Chesca bowls off uncontested and the soft ground slows the pace enough that her lead holds to the line.
scenarios.body: She dictates every yard, setting a gallop that is taxing but not suicidal, and the soft ground rewards her front-running brand of stamina; hold-up horses lack the ground and the furlong count to pick her up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Runs Her Down
scenarios.trigger: If Eleven Eighty Two or an unknown debutante travels smoothly just off the pace and produces a late surge that swamps the tiring leader in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Soft ground strips the leader's advantage as her stamina is tested, and a horse who has conserved energy a length or two off the pace has enough momentum to mow her down; Eleven Eighty Two's twice-placed 6f form suggests she can quicken when given a target.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutante Surprises From Unknown
scenarios.trigger: If one of the well-bred debutantes — Floral Maid, Pivotal Voyage, or Get On That Baby — possesses a natural prominent style and bounces out with controlled early pace to land a maiden blow.
scenarios.body: Trainers of talent in soft-ground maidens often produce first-time-out youngsters well, and a debutante with a genuine front-running tendency could slot straight into the ideal tactical position behind Cheeky Chesca.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground produces an unusually slow, stop-start gallop that collapses in the final furlong and leaves the field bunched, giving closers a rare chance to finish through.
scenarios.body: Even in this scenario, the true hold-up horses such as Dawn's Gift, Last Dandelion, and Dorothea Hope are all racing out of their natural role and will struggle to secure the wide, clean passage a genuine closer needs over five furlongs; this remains the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Cheeky Chesca's draw and early jump are critical — if she exits cleanly and hits the front within the first furlong, her uncontested lead on soft ground makes her very hard to peg back.
Eleven Eighty Two drops to 5f for the first time; if the trip proves too sharp in soft ground she may not sustain her effort, which would open the door for a prominent debutante to fill the gap.

Picnic Princess and Pivotal Voyage are unexposed debutantes from pace-savvy yards (Fahey, Ryan) — watch early market moves as money for either could signal a natural front-running or prominent style that suits the race shape perfectly.

With six confirmed hold-up types scrambling for midfield positions, there is a significant risk of traffic issues and interference inside the final two furlongs — horses drawn high (wider berths) may be at a slight advantage in finding a clear run.

Soft ground at Beverley on a full card — monitor any ground softening through the afternoon; if conditions worsen further, early position becomes even more of a premium and the hold-up brigade's chances diminish further.

races.name: Ward Homes Yorkshire Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Golden Redemption
runners_data.note: Habitual hold-up performer for Harker who has been running over shorter trips on good ground recently; the step up in distance on soft at Beverley suits in theory but the 57-day absence and lack of any soft-ground wins in recent form makes this a speculative each-way play at best.

runners_data.name: Count Palatine
runners_data.note: Dods has the yard in form (4/23 over 14 days) and this horse has a soft-ground win on his card (sim-going: 2W 2P), races prominently, and comes back from just 11 days off in good nick; the step up to 1m½f on today's soft conditions looks tailor-made.

runners_data.name: On The River
runners_data.note: Bethell's seven-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse with strong soft-ground credentials (10/15 sim-going strikes), but the congested rear means he is unlikely to get his natural berth and will need to race further forward than ideal, which tempers confidence even if the stamina and going are right.

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed pace-setters, Rawlinson takes the mount for Tuer whose yard is quiet (0/12 over 14 days); the horse's sim-going record at just 1/15 with no wins or places is a significant red flag, and soft ground looks like a real question mark for a horse whose best form has come on good.

runners_data.name: Priapos
runners_data.note: Makin's four-year-old holds the highest OR in the field at 85 and has back-to-back wins on his card, but both came on good ground and his soft-going exposure is minimal (1/15, no wins or places); a hold-up horse who will need the pace to truly collapse for his late run to land.

runners_data.name: Nostrum
runners_data.note: Appleby runner flagged for fading in the finish, which is a serious concern on soft ground over this trip at the end of a race run at a stiff pace; the recent form string (025800) is uninspiring and the sim-going record offers no encouragement.

runners_data.name: Walsingham
runners_data.note: O'Meara runner who has produced one soft-ground win and four places from six sim-going runs, suggesting the conditions are not a hindrance, but the recent form (108057) shows only a distant win and a raft of disappointing efforts; races from the rear and needs a strong pace to suit.

runners_data.name: Hot Cash
runners_data.note: Channon's four-year-old has a soft-ground placing and was placed twice on good, running prominently; the 36-day break is not alarming, but OR 83 and a form string of -02280 suggests he is below peak at present.

runners_data.name: Tele Red
runners_data.note: Burke's nine-year-old has excellent soft-ground and heavy form credentials (7/15 sim-going, 1W 4P), races prominently, and the recent form over 10 furlongs on soft (2-1-2 in his last three outings) reads like a horse who thrives in these exact conditions; the 310-day absence is the one clear risk.

runners_data.name: Wondrous Light
runners_data.note: Stott partners this Portman four-year-old who has outstanding soft-going form: three wins and four places from 13 sim-going runs, including back-to-back wins on soft and a placed effort on soft in recent form; a prominent runner who handles this ground better than most in the field.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: Loughnane's filly has won four of her last six but notably only 2/15 sim-going strikes and just one soft-ground placing in her last run; the tongue-tie is noted, but soft ground looks a genuine query for a horse who does her best work on quicker surfaces.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Easterby's five-year-old is a natural hold-up horse who has been shuffled into a midfield mapping because the back of the field is oversubscribed; soft-ground exposure is limited (2/15, no wins or places), and the style compromise means this is a harder race for him to win than his OR of 76 might suggest.

runners_data.name: Panelli
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner alongside Highland Olly; Hardie takes the ride for Sowersby who is quiet (0/4 over 14 days), and the horse's own soft-going record is virtually blank (1/15, no wins or places) — setting the pace on testing ground over this trip without the ability to handle conditions is a risky proposition.

races.paceDynamic: Highland Olly and Panelli are the two confirmed front-runners here, and with both likely to press for the early lead on soft ground over 1m½f at Beverley, this race will be run at an honest, energy-sapping gallop from the outset — neither is the type to ease off once in front. The prominent contingent of Count Palatine, Hot Cash, Tele Red, Wondrous Light, and The Sweet Escape will be hunting positions just off the pace, adding further competitive pressure through the early and middle stages, which means the gallop is unlikely to relent. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can all secure their natural position — Highland Olly and Panelli are almost certain to lead, while On The River and Financer, both genuine hold-up horses, have been mapped to midfield because the rear is oversubscribed, meaning their true closer's role is compromised. A strong, unrelenting gallop on soft ground over this trip will drain the leaders in the closing stages, and the profile that benefits most clearly is the patient, well-stamina'd hold-up or late-prominent type who can travel within themselves and finish strongly when others are emptying — soft-ground form and genuine stamina for the trip are the key qualifiers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop, Stayers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Highland Olly and Panelli force a genuine end-to-end pace on soft ground that grinds down the prominent types.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a punishing tempo that burns through the prominent challengers, leaving the race wide open for those who have settled mid-to-rear and can unleash stamina-backed finishes in the closing furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is competitive but not truly brutal, allowing horses racing prominently to sit within striking range and sustain their efforts to the line.
scenarios.body: A contested but manageable early gallop sees the front-runners tire without blowing up the race entirely, and prominent runners with soft-ground form who have settled just off the pace find the most favourable ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Escapes
scenarios.trigger: If one of Highland Olly or Panelli breaks clear and the other falls tamely away, leaving an uncontested lead through the middle part of the race.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner who is allowed to coast on soft ground can dictate tempo and steal enough of a buffer that the hold-up types, forced wide or unable to quicken on the testing surface, cannot bridge the gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so fierce that it fully shreds the prominent types and the race falls apart dramatically in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A race run at a truly severe gallop can leave the track clear for horses finishing from the rear, though On The River and Financer — both natural closers — are not guaranteed to be in their optimal position in this race shape, limiting the likelihood of this outcome.

watchPoints.text: Tele Red has outstanding soft-ground form (7/15 sim-going, 1W 4P, two recent wins on soft) and races prominently, but a 310-day absence is the single biggest risk factor to monitor — watch how he handles the early pressure in the market and in the first furlong to gauge fitness.

Wondrous Light's soft-going record is exceptional (3W 4P from 13 runs) and she sits at OR 76 with a prominent style that suits this pace shape — if the market shortens her late, treat it seriously as the going is a strong personal asset.

Highland Olly and Panelli both have near-blank soft-ground records (1/15 combined, no wins or places between them), meaning the two horses tasked with setting a strong pace are racing on ground that may not suit them — watch for either weakening sharply from the 3f pole, which could scramble the race shape entirely.

On The River and Financer are genuine hold-up horses who will be racing closer to the pace than they prefer due to the congested rear of the field — if neither can settle in a true closing position, their soft-ground credentials may be rendered irrelevant by the positional compromise.

Count Palatine runs back just 11 days after a win on soft (sim-going: 2W 2P) for an in-form Dods yard (4/23 over 14 days) — connections clearly believe the horse is thriving and the recency is a positive rather than a concern.

races.name: Constant Security Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Managing Director
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front runner here; Geoff Oldroyd's four-year-old has one soft-ground win at this course and trip combination (1/9 in similar going), and P J McDonald's quiet, efficient front-running style suits a horse who is most dangerous when allowed to bowl along without a shadow on his shoulder.

runners_data.name: Holbache
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's eight-year-old is a seasoned handicapper with 2W3P from 15 starts in similar going conditions, and Tom Kiely-Marshall (5) rides with a claim; headgear noted (p) and the horse wants to be prominent — if he finds a clean passage from the gate the soft ground and experience could make him dangerous late.

runners_data.name: Military Girl
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners Michael Dods' four-year-old who boasts two wins and a second from five recent starts at 5f on good, and while soft ground is untested in her record she arrives with sharp in-form figures from a powerful yard — her prominent style maps perfectly to what this race shape rewards.

runners_data.name: Daizen
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' three-year-old won over 6f on good and has soft-ground entries in his history; Andrew Mullen takes the ride but recent form includes wide-margin defeats and his soft-going record (6th, 5th from two runs) raises an honest question about how well he handles cut in the ground.

runners_data.name: Ventura Express
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's nine-year-old specialises in this track and trip but has recorded 4th, 4th, 6th, 4th, 4th across his last five — consistent without threatening — and David Nolan will hold him up, which on a day when prominent horses are favoured makes him a watch-and-wait type rather than a pace influence.

runners_data.name: Qila
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's three-year-old is tagged with trial headgear and has placed twice in six soft-ground starts; M P Sheehy takes the ride and the horse wants to race prominently, but a form string showing no wins and a tendency to fade late on soft (10th at 5f soft) tempers optimism about the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Tiriac
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan partners Paul Midgley's six-year-old, who arrives 29 days between runs and carries headgear (p); his soft-going record reads 7th from five comparable starts and his hold-up style is at odds with today's prominent-favoured shape, making him a longer-shot beneficiary of any chaos rather than a primary contender.

runners_data.name: Tees Aggregates
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls' four-year-old carries the trainer's three-pound claimer Jack Nicholls and has a soft-ground placing to his name (3/5f/SOF); his last three runs are poor but the drop back to conditions where he once placed and a short 13-day turnaround from a fresh yard suggest he merits some respect if the soft ground becomes a leveller.

runners_data.name: Great
runners_data.note: Sam England's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by style and has two wins on his recent record, though both came on good ground; Shane Gray rides and the absence of any soft-ground evidence in his history is the key unknown — if the ground is within his range he could emerge wide, but the style is out of sync with what today rewards.

runners_data.name: Miss Brazen
runners_data.note: Michael and David Easterby's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up performer by nature — that is her true style — though she is mapped to midfield here because the rear of the field is already crowded with similar types; Joanna Mason rides and the horse's best form (1/5f/GOO) came on faster ground, so the combination of positional compromise and soft conditions is a double difficulty.

runners_data.name: Simba's Pride
runners_data.note: Mark Winn partners Michael Dods' three-year-old, who wants to be prominent and arrives from the same in-form yard as Military Girl; his recent form string (154347) shows a tendency to run into the placings rather than win, and on soft ground without any similar-conditions evidence the risk is that he gets shuffled back in the prominent scrimmage.

runners_data.name: Ice Cold Alex
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears' three-year-old is by nature a hold-up horse — his true preference is to come from off the pace — but surplus hold-up types in this field mean he is likely to find himself racing in a midfield position that neither suits his relaxed style nor gives him a late-run platform; Cam Hardie rides and three soft-ground runs have returned a best of 4th.

runners_data.name: Empress Olivia
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's three-year-old is lightly weighted and prominent in style but all five recent runs have come on good ground and show no wins since the opening run on the card; Dougie Costello rides but the 33-day absence and complete lack of soft-ground evidence makes this a genuine unknown that the market will likely ignore.

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old is a natural prominent racer at heart — that is where he does his best work — but with more prominent types than slots available he is mapped to midfield and David Allan is unlikely to be able to retrieve his preferred ground; the 36-day absence and a sim-going record of 0W0P from 15 starts in similar conditions compound the concern.

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's seven-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, though the surplus of similar types has pushed him to a midfield mapping he will need to adapt to; Jason Hart rides and his best soft-ground effort is a 2/5f/SOF, which is at least relevant form — if he gets a clear sight of daylight in the final furlong rather than being caught in traffic he could outperform his odds.

races.paceDynamic: Managing Director is the lone confirmed front runner and, with no genuine rival forcing the pace from the gates, is set to dictate at a controlled, pressure-free tempo on soft ground at Beverley — a track where early position is already at a premium on the five-furlong trip. Behind him, Holbache, Military Girl, Daizen, Qila, Simba's Pride and Empress Olivia all want prominent positions, creating a congested battle for the early slots from two to six that will compress the chasing pack and generate lateral traffic danger between the two- and three-furlong markers. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically all get their preferred position; Managing Director is certain to lead, with Military Girl and Holbache the most likely to physically secure the next slots given draw, rider experience and recent sharp form, while Dream Deal, though a natural prominent racer, has been redistributed to midfield and is unlikely to get his preferred ground. Soft ground on a stiff five furlongs at Beverley historically rewards horses who travel prominently with cover and sustain their effort through the final climb, making a clean prominent berth the profile most likely to produce the winner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Managing Director bowls along unchallenged and the prominent pack gets entangled settling positions, robbing them of momentum.
scenarios.body: Managing Director dictates a soft but sustainable tempo, finds the soft ground within his comfort zone given his one prior win at this track, and the prominent congestion behind him means rivals lose ground changing positions rather than mounting a coordinated challenge; a horse who can slot in second or third on his girth without burning energy is perfectly placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent type secures a clean position just off Managing Director and has enough left to collar him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The congestion between the prominent runners resolves early enough for one horse — most likely Military Girl or Holbache, both of whom have course-and-distance or 5f soft-ground form — to travel smoothly in the first two and unleash a sustained challenge in the final two furlongs on the energy-sapping surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Robs Front Rank
scenarios.trigger: If the soft going saps the front runners in the final furlong and a midfield tracker produces a strong late surge.
scenarios.body: Ventura Express or Tees Aggregates, both of whom have soft-ground form at the trip and prefer to be held up slightly, could be produced with a run if the leaders tie up; the stiff Beverley five does tend to find out horses who have run too freely, but the lack of genuine pace makes a true late surge hard to execute.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Creates Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion in the first two furlongs causes a pile-up of checked horses and a wide runner or a horse forced widest emerges late.
scenarios.body: A horse that is drawn wide or sent outside the tangle — possibly Great or Tiriac emerging from the rear — could benefit if the prominent pack checks each other and the pace collapses simultaneously; this is a low-probability shape because the going rewards those who get cover, not those who loop the field.

watchPoints.text: Managing Director — watch whether P J McDonald is challenged from the gate; if a prominent rival pushes across to dispute early, the soft ground could extract a heavier price and turn a tactical advantage into vulnerability.

Prominent congestion — Military Girl, Holbache, Daizen, Qila and Simba's Pride all want positions two through six, and the scramble between the two- and three-furlong poles is the single biggest traffic danger in the race; any horse caught wide or checked at that point loses vital momentum on soft ground.

Dream Deal — a natural prominent racer forced wide and back by the sheer weight of pace types in this field; David Allan may attempt to hunt up into contention, and if he does so aggressively he risks burning petrol that leaves the horse empty at the furlong pole.

Ventura Express — nine years old, hold-up style, five consecutive fourths suggest a horse that is filling the frame without troubling the winner; watch whether David Nolan attempts to switch his run wider than usual if the inside is a wall of horses.

Soft ground watch — the going report confirms soft across all 5f races today at Beverley; horses without any evidence of handling cut (Great, Empress Olivia, Military Girl) are worth monitoring in the early stages to see whether they travel with their usual fluency or are niggled along sooner than expected.

races.name: Return Of The Legend Martin Spencer Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Printing Money
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Dylan Cunha, last run 11 days ago; all recent form on Good or Standard ground with no soft experience confirmed, though no going concern flagged — needs significant improvement on a best of third.|

runners_data.name: Nosey Book
runners_data.note: Sean Kirrane rides this Tim Easterby prominent racer who placed third on this track over 7f; stepping up from 7f to 7½f is a logical progression and soft ground appears untroubling — this trip and pace setup suits.|

runners_data.name: Sunrise At Dawn
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's 2yo has soft-ground form (finished 5th over 5f on soft) and has won at this trip class before; a natural hold-up runner who, given the volume of closers in this field, is unlikely to secure its preferred rearward position — treat its market position accordingly.|

runners_data.name: Black Fury
runners_data.note: Cam Hardie takes the mount on this Ollie Pears prominent type who has placed twice from three runs; Goodwood and Catterick form stepping to soft at Beverley is a minor query, but the consistent placed record suggests a reliable racing style that can take advantage of a clean run.|

runners_data.name: Inns And Out
runners_data.note: David Allan on a Tim Easterby hold-up type who won over 7f at Goodwood last time out and returns just 5 days later — quick turnaround for a trainer in excellent form (5/85 in 14 days); genuinely strong recent form makes this one of the most interesting closers in the field.|

runners_data.name: Bella Lucia
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's 5-day going-concern flag is absent but the STYLE_FIT tag indicates she may not fully replicate her natural leading role here; a confirmed front-runner holding a course-winning entry, she has placed on soft before and Conor Whiteley claims 5lbs — her ability to control the fractions unchallenged is the race's central question.|

runners_data.name: Amantha
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners this Brian Ellison hold-up type who won over 7f at Goodwood and has six runs of consistently placed form; all career runs on Good ground raises a soft-going question, but Ellison's 8-day turnaround suggests confidence — the step to 7½f on testing ground is the key stamina test.|

runners_data.name: Court Legend
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason on Michael & David Easterby's hold-up runner who carries a hood and has placed second over 8f; the 0502 recent form is inconsistent and two tenth-place finishes at 6f suggest trip was a factor — this extra furlong and soft ground may suit better.|

runners_data.name: Scarlet Dynasty
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's lower-rated closer carries both a fade-in-finish warning and is a genuine hold-up horse shifted into the midfield position on the map because the field is loaded with closers — its true position will be further back, compounding the finishing concern flagged in its form.|

runners_data.name: Tiger In The Tree
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up type is naturally rearward but the crowded closer's market means it too is displaced forward on the pace map; carries hood, returns after 30 days, and three recent placed runs over 7-8f on Good ground give a platform, but soft ground is unproven and its natural position is unlikely to be available.|

runners_data.name: Be More Ruthless
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls runner ridden by son Jack (3lb claim) with a fade-in-finish flag; prominent style but three consecutive bottom-end finishes (5th, 11th, 10th) give little confidence — if it gets a prominent berth the soft ground and tendency to fade make it a vulnerability rather than a threat.|

runners_data.name: Loveulongtime
runners_data.note: William Pyle rides this Geoffrey Harker prominent type at a career-low OR of 47; form of 7048 is uninspiring, the best effort a fourth over 5f on Good ground, and stepping to 7½f soft looks a significant test of stamina for a horse that has not suggested it stays this far.|

races.paceDynamic: Bella Lucia is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner nursery over 7½f on soft ground at Beverley, and with no genuine rival pressing her for the lead, she is likely to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo from the front. Nosey Book and Black Fury will push into prominent positions just off Bella Lucia's shoulder, creating a small lead group but no serious pace battle — the absence of pressure means fractions will be measured rather than frenetic on testing ground. The soft going will stretch this field out quickly and reward horses who settle into a rhythm early and travel efficiently, which tilts the advantage firmly toward the prominent-to-midfield profile that can get a clean run off a steady pace and produce a sustained finish rather than a sudden sprint. Inns And Out, Amantha, and Court Legend are the genuine hold-up types sitting at the rear, and while the map shows Sunrise At Dawn, Tiger In The Tree, and Scarlet Dynasty in midfield, all three are true hold-up horses redistributed forward in the diagram because the field has more closers than the shape can honestly accommodate — Bella Lucia, Nosey Book, and Black Fury are most likely to actually secure their natural positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bella Lucia Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Bella Lucia meets no pace pressure and dictates a soft-ground gallop from the front with a clear lead.
scenarios.body: Bella Lucia sets a measured, energy-conserving tempo on testing ground, and the horses who travel prominently just behind her — Nosey Book and Black Fury — are ideally placed to capitalise as the field strings out in the home straight; genuine closers face too much ground to make up against a leader who was never challenged.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collar The Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Nosey Book or Black Fury track Bella Lucia closely and have enough in reserve to reel her in across the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The soft ground saps Bella Lucia's advantage as the race develops and the horses sitting second or third with cover find the stamina edge over a tiring leader; this scenario suits horses with a strong staying profile who have been dropping in from further trips.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the closing stages and a closer finds a clear gap to finish powerfully past a tired front group.
scenarios.body: A genuine stay in the lead means the field compresses late when Bella Lucia falters, and a hold-up type who has settled well and saved energy on soft ground can produce a sustained run; Amantha is best placed here given recent winning form over 7f and a proven trainer-jockey combination, with Inns And Out also a realistic finisher having won over 7f at Goodwood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Causes Bunching
scenarios.trigger: If Black Fury or Nosey Book pushes forward aggressively early and creates genuine pressure on Bella Lucia, unsettling the pace shape.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace battle on soft ground will exhaust the principals quickly, opening the door for a horse who races midfield in a chaotic scenario; this is a low-probability shape because there is no strong evidence of intent from the prominent pair to race boldly, but Amantha and Court Legend would be the beneficiaries if it materialised.

watchPoints.text: Bella Lucia — if Conor Whiteley (5lb claimer) misjudges the tempo on soft ground and goes too fast too early, the entire prominent-runner scenario unravels and opens the race to late closers like Amantha and Inns And Out.

Inns And Out — racing just 5 days after its last run is a quick turnaround; if the horse carries any residual fatigue from its winning effort at Goodwood it may not see out the extra 7½f on testing ground despite strong form.

Amantha — all six career runs have come on Good ground and this is its first encounter with soft; Brian Ellison's confidence is noted, but genuine soft-ground inexperience at a crucial moment in the race is a live risk.

Tiger In The Tree, Sunrise At Dawn, Scarlet Dynasty — all three are genuine hold-up types who cannot realistically claim their preferred position in this field shape; if they are crowded wide or forced to race too freely chasing the pace, their chances diminish further than form alone would suggest.

Court Legend (hood) and Tiger In The Tree (hood) — both carry headgear and both have shown inconsistency; on a day when soft ground and a controlled pace may expose non-triers, the hood-wearing horses bear monitoring in running for early signs of effort or lack thereof.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Hull Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Elemental Eye
runners_data.note: Won over 12f at Stratford last time, handles soft, and has placed twice in similar going conditions — a genuine hold-up type who will need more pace ahead than Punxsutawney Phil is likely to provide, and at 55 days since last run is reasonably fresh; blinkers applied.

runners_data.name: Marbuzet
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with modest recent form including a ninth last time at Sandown, has just one placing in 15 runs in similar going, and at OR=67 is near the top of the weights — a natural hold-up horse who will be frustrated by the expected absence of a strong gallop to aim at.

runners_data.name: Time Turner
runners_data.note: Four-year-old in fair recent form (194523 string) for Edward Bethell, a trainer firing well at 7/28 over 14 days — genuinely wants to come from off the pace, but with four other true closers in the field he is likely to end up racing in midfield rather than the rear, meaning his natural finishing kick may be blunted by traffic and early energy expended.

runners_data.name: Pfingstberg
runners_data.note: Six-year-old returning from 696 days off for Mark Walford — a long layoff is the dominant concern, but his form before that break shows a win and two placed efforts over this trip on soft-to-similar ground, and as the only genuine prominent runner behind the leader he occupies a tactically favourable position if his fitness holds.

runners_data.name: Shopaholic
runners_data.note: Recent form shows a third at Sandown last time, and the horse has one soft-ground outing to its name; a true hold-up type that will find itself in midfield rather than its natural rear position given the field composition, which is a meaningful structural disadvantage in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Spooky Wooky
runners_data.note: Has placed on soft going at 15f and handles this kind of ground, but the pace scenario here is the problem — finishing third and second in his best efforts came in stronger-run races, and being pushed into a midfield slot rather than the back of the field dilutes the chance he can produce his characteristic late run.

runners_data.name: Punxsutawney Phil
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the pivotal horse in this race — two wins from nine soft-ground starts and proven over 20f plus, though 527 days off the track is an obvious fitness flag; if Walford has him ready, the pace map runs entirely through him.

runners_data.name: Jedhi Knight
runners_data.note: Ten days since last run is the freshest in the field, and he has won over 12f on good ground, but soft conditions and stepping up markedly in trip are uncharted territory — another genuine hold-up horse operating in midfield by necessity, meaning his best chance relies on a race shape this field is structurally unlikely to produce.

races.paceDynamic: Punxsutawney Phil is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field over 2m on soft ground at Beverley, and with no meaningful challenger for the lead, he should dictate from the front at a tempo entirely of his own choosing — almost certainly a measured, energy-conserving gallop that plays directly to his stamina strengths on ground he handles. Pfingstberg is the only other runner with prominent tendencies and could sit just behind, but even that pairing leaves the bulk of the field in a trailing pack with limited cover and a long way to travel. The soft going over this marathon trip will put a premium on relaxed jumping-off ability, stamina reserves, and timing of challenge — conditions that should test hold-up horses who need a strong pace to aim at and will instead find a slow-motion leader pulling the strings. This race shape strongly favours Punxsutawney Phil and any horse able to sit close enough to the measured gallop without over-racing, rather than deep closers who need genuine pace to reel in. The field holds more true hold-up types than can realistically operate from their natural position — Time Turner, Shopaholic, Spooky Wooky, and Jedhi Knight are all genuine rear-runners mapped to midfield, with Elemental Eye and Marbuzet the only credible hold-up horses likely to find anything like their natural ground; the most probable outcome is that several of these closers find themselves shuffled into uncomfortable midfield roles with too little pace ahead to challenge from.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Punxsutawney Phil Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Punxsutawney Phil leads uncontested and sets a soft, stamina-sapping pace on the soft ground.
scenarios.body: Punxsutawney Phil bowls along in front with Pfingstberg tracking second, and the field strings out behind with no pressure applied — soft ground and a crawl turns the final half-mile into a stamina slog that the leader, fresh from a long break and proven over this trip and going, is perfectly placed to exploit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Pfingstberg or a horse sitting handy tracks the slow pace and produces a decisive kick approaching the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: With the pace modest, a horse who has settled just off Punxsutawney Phil's shoulder conserves energy through the soft ground and has enough left to reel in the leader late — Pfingstberg, with proven form over this trip and going, is the natural candidate in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften up the leader and one of the true closers finds room to finish with purpose.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected pace from Punxsutawney Phil, perhaps encouraged by Pfingstberg pressing harder, could create a target for a fresh closer — Elemental Eye, who has won over similar distances and handles soft, is the likeliest beneficiary, though the redistributed nature of most hold-up runners here means timing a late run is structurally harder than in a truly strong-pace race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Weakens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the long absence (527 days) leaves Punxsutawney Phil underdone for fitness and he ties up in the final quarter-mile of soft ground.
scenarios.body: A horse who has led a slow race but lacks race-fitness fades dramatically late, opening the door for anything sitting handy — Pfingstberg, the only other prominent type with course and distance form, is best positioned, though the hold-up pack would still need to find gears they haven't been set up to find.

watchPoints.text: Punxsutawney Phil's 527-day absence is the single biggest variable in this race — if he is underdone for fitness, the race shape collapses entirely and any horse sitting handy benefits immediately.

Pfingstberg is also returning after 696 days off the track, meaning both of the horses expected to lead or sit prominent carry significant fitness question marks that could scramble the anticipated race shape.

With Time Turner, Shopaholic, Spooky Wooky, and Jedhi Knight all true hold-up types forced into midfield, watch for early crowding and traffic issues as the field settles in the first half-mile — a slowly-run race with a bunched midfield on soft ground is a recipe for interference.

Elemental Eye (blinkers, 55 days fresh) and Marbuzet are the only hold-up runners not tagged as redistributed — they are the two closers best placed to operate closest to their natural style, and if either can find a pocket off a genuinely slow pace, they represent the most credible late threat.
